projectName: MCP Stdio Server — Bitcoin Treasury Tools
description: Expose the Bitcoin Accounting data layer as a read-only MCP stdio server so AI clients (primarily Claude Desktop) can query treasury details, capital gains, tax summaries, and integrity health directly. Primary use case: financial planning, mid-year tax optimization, and 1099-B generation awareness.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature-16 (Treasury Attestation Monitoring) merged to master — provides integrity/attestation modules this feature consumes.

principles: Read-only: zero write operations via MCP — all mutations stay in the TUI
Minimal surface: 10 focused tools covering portfolio, tax, integrity, and attestation
Thin wrapper: reuse existing BitcoinAccounts and integrity/attestation APIs unchanged
Async-safe: synchronous DB layer wrapped in asyncio.to_thread() per call, open/close per tool invocation
Financial planning first: tax and capital gains tools are the highest-value group for the Claude Desktop use case

techStack.runtime: MCP stdio server (bitcoin-mcp CLI entry point)

testingRequirements.unitTests: Mock BitcoinAccounts and backend; test each tool's return shape, error handling, and edge cases in isolation
testingRequirements.integrationTests: Start FastMCP test client; call each tool end-to-end against a real in-memory SQLite DB
testingRequirements.edgeCases: Empty snapshot table (get_treasury_health), quantity<=0 (forecast_capital_gains), invalid month (get_attestation_bundle), limit capping (get_transactions), missing price data (get_purchase_lots)
testingRequirements.ci: All 4 story test files must pass with no asyncio warnings

fileStructure.description: Single new source file plus a test file. Two lines change in pyproject.toml. No changes to existing modules.

src/python/.mcp_server.py: NEW — FastMCP server with 10 read-only tools, helpers, and main()

tests/.test_mcp_server.py: NEW — unit and integration tests for all 10 tools

layout.pyproject.toml: MODIFIED — add mcp dep, add bitcoin-mcp entry point

connection_lifecycle.decision: Open a fresh DatabaseBackend per tool call inside asyncio.to_thread(); close in finally block
connection_lifecycle.rationale: Matches the existing CLI pattern. Avoids shared-state concurrency issues. For a stdio server with a single AI client the overhead is acceptable.

no_write_tools.decision: Expose zero write/mutate operations (no deposit, withdraw, record_trade, etc.)
no_write_tools.rationale: Keeps the MCP surface safe for untrusted AI use. All mutations go through the TUI with human confirmation. The AI can advise; the human executes.

tax_year_current.decision: get_tax_summary accepts any tax_year including the current year
tax_year_current.rationale: Mid-year realized gains are the primary financial planning use case. Passing the current year returns partial-year 1099-B data which Claude Desktop can use to advise on tax exposure.
tax_year_current.example: get_tax_summary(tax_year=2026) returns YTD realized gains for planning

purchase_lots_unrealized.decision: get_purchase_lots fetches current price via price_lookup and computes unrealized P&L per lot
purchase_lots_unrealized.rationale: This is the foundation for tax-optimal selling advice. Knowing which lots are short-term vs long-term with their unrealized gain/loss lets Claude suggest which to sell first.
purchase_lots_unrealized.example: {acquire_date, quantity, unit_cost, current_price, unrealized_pnl, holding_days, term: Short|Long}

serialize_helper.decision: Single _serialize() recursive helper converts datetime/date/Decimal before returning from each tool
serialize_helper.rationale: FastMCP serializes return values to JSON; Python datetime and Decimal are not JSON-native. Centralizing conversion avoids repetition across 10 tools.
